Captions.text: Team 28: Pitstop is healthy. We test resilience only in our own local Docker sandbox.
Dependency map: three APIs share SQL Server; RabbitMQ connects the background services.
Recorded real Qwen run: the AI ranked experiments from this map and the healthy baseline. All three ran and recovered.
Live safety demonstration: fixed-order Workshop crash plus bounded GET traffic. Two connections, 10 requests/sec, no writes.
Automatic discovery reviews baseline measurements, incident history and dependency risks. Only registered tools can execute.
Failure is real: Workshop shows the offline fallback. HTTP 200 alone is not a healthy result.
Customer remains available: this single-service failure is isolated. The runner measures content and response times.
Emergency STOP requests early rollback. The independent watchdog and threshold limits remain armed.
Workshop is healthy again. Verified recovery and the traffic measurements are retained as JSON and CSV.
The completed AI suite covers service crash, shared database outage and network delay. Threshold rollback and recovery are recorded.
Real model findings rank weaknesses and recommend fixes, linked to measured anomaly IDs. AI explanations need human review.
Fix and retest: a two-second request budget gives faster fallback without replaying writes. Faster failure is not restored availability.
Submission includes source, this captioned demo, one-page architecture, ranked findings and Team 28 details.

Note: Real live combined fault and STOP recovery; AI ranking/findings shown from a previous completed real model run.
